title: Mario Is Named After Nintendo's Landlord
hook: Nintendo of America named Donkey Kong's hero after Mario Segale, the man who rented it a warehouse near Seattle in the early 1980s, and this week his creator Shigeru Miyamoto became the first ever DICE Legend Award inductee. Would you name your hero after your landlord?
script: Did you know Mario is named after a real landlord? In the early nineteen eighties, Nintendo of America was a small operation renting a warehouse in Tukwila, Washington, just outside Seattle. The owner was a local real estate developer named Mario Segale. Nintendo's new arcade hit Donkey Kong starred a hero called Jumpman, and the American team wanted him to have a proper name. They picked their landlord's. The famous version of the story says Segale had just stormed in demanding overdue rent, though that part has never been confirmed. Either way, the name stuck. Segale never leaned into it. In nineteen ninety three he told the Seattle Times he was still waiting for his royalty checks. He stayed away from the spotlight for the rest of his life, and he passed away in twenty eighteen at age eighty four. Shigeru Miyamoto finally confirmed the name's origin on camera in twenty fifteen. And this week Miyamoto himself made news. On November sixteenth, the Academy of Interactive Arts and Sciences named him the first ever Legend Award inductee. That honor will be given out no more than once a decade. He receives it at the DICE Awards in February. Would you name your hero after your landlord? Follow for more gaming history.
